items.title: Relative pseudo-coherence is preserved by derived base change along a relatively pseudo-coherent algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the compatibility of relative pseudo-coherence with derived base change: for finite type ring maps R -> A -> B with B pseudo-coherent relative to A, an m-pseudo-coherent (or pseudo-coherent) complex K over R stays so after the derived tensor product with B (statement lines 21567-21576). The proof rewrites the derived base change through a finite free resolution of B over a polynomial algebra, obtaining a total complex over R, and then filters that total complex by the shifted complexes K tensor_A E^i so that the cone criterion reduces the problem to a single case which is the base change along a polynomial algebra (proof lines 21578-21618). The two nontrivial moves are the rewriting of the derived base change as a total complex and the filtration argument, and both are inside the counted span. The proof refers three times to earlier lemmas of the same chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
